item.title: Causal mediation analysis of contact with COVID-19 patients and burnout syndrome in physiotherapists in Japan: secondary analysis of a multicentre observational study.
item.description: This study looked at Japanese physiotherapists who worked with COVID-19 patients and found that direct contact with patients contributed to burnout, but this effect was partly buffered by appreciation and respect from patients and colleagues. The study suggests that organisational resources, such as reimbursement for care, may also play a role in burnout. Burnout prevalence was 19.4% among the physiotherapists.

item.title: Adrenal Function in Critical Illness
item.description: This study looked at how often adrenal insufficiency happens in critically ill patients and why it's a problem. They found that it occurs in up to 77% of cases, but there's no standard way to diagnose it. Researchers need to figure out how to identify and treat adrenal insufficiency.

item.title: THE ROLE OF PANCREATIC STONE PROTEIN (PSP) AND PSP-GUIDED EARLY MEROPENEM TREATMENT TO MITIGATE SEPSIS RISK AT THE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT: THE PROMISE DOUBLE BLIND, PHASE III, RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED CLINICAL TRIAL
item.description: The goal of this clinical trial is to demonstrate the clinical benefit of early intervention with meropenem in adult patients of both sexes with suspected infection and risk of sepsis. The primary objective is to evaluate the clinical benefit of a protein called Pancreatic Stone Protein (PSP), which, if elevated, indicates that patient may be at increased risk of developing sepsis. item.description: This study aims to investigate whether combining cycling exercise with an immersive and interactive virtual reality (VR) environment improves motivation compared with cycling without visual support or cycling while watching a route on a television screen in critically ill patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU). item.title: A Phase III, Open Label, Randomized, Controlled Study of VBI-S in the Treatment of Hypovolemia in Patients With Septic Shock (VBI-S-02)
item.description: This study is being conducted to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of VBI-S in elevating the blood pressure of septic shock patients with absolute or relative hypovolemia.

item.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Readmission Reduction Interventions for Individuals With Sepsis or Pneumonia
item.description: An adaptive platform trial to compare effectiveness of different care models to prevent readmissions for patients hospitalized with sepsis or lower respiratory tract infection. The primary outcome is number of days spent at home within 90 days after hospital discharge.

item.description: Septic shock is a syndrome associated with severe infection and a mortality rate of approximately 45%. In line with current recommendations, norepinephrine is the first-line vasopressor used in patients with septic shock. In a previous study, norepinephrine doses above 1 µg/kg/min were associated with mortality rates over 90%. In the same study, doses above 0.3 µg/kg/min were associated with a mortality rate of 40%. item.title: Respiratory Physiotherapy and PMR After Cardiac Surgery
item.description: This study aims to evaluate the effects of respiratory physiotherapy combined with progressive muscle relaxation exercises on dyspnea, anxiety, hemodynamic status, and delirium symptoms in patients after cardiac surgery. This randomized controlled trial will include 116 patients who will be randomly assigned to an intervention group or a control group. item.title: Characterization and Longitudinal Monitoring of Muscular Phenotype in Patients Admitted to Intensive Care for Sepsis
item.description: Approximately 40% of patients develop muscle dysfunction during their stay in intensive care, particularly in the context of sepsis. This dysfunction represents an acquired muscle injury that is secondary to the primary illness that led to ICU admission. It affects both the limb muscles and the respiratory muscles of the thoracic cage. item.description: Bacteremia, a common infection associated with high morbidity and mortality, requires prompt and appropriate antibiotic treatment. Numerous studies have shown that the appropriate use of antibiotics helps improve the prognosis of patients, reduce the selection of pathogenic organisms, the emergence of antibiotic resistance, adverse treatment effects, and healthcare costs. item.title: Physiological Dead Space and Intensive Care Mortality in Mechanically Ventilated Patients
item.description: This study investigates the relationship between physiological dead space and clinical outcomes, specifically mortality and discharge status, in adult patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation in the intensive care unit (ICU). Physiological dead space refers to ventilated but non-perfused regions of the lungs and can be quantified using the Enghoff-modified Bohr equation based on capnographic and arterial CO₂ measurements. item.description: The purpose of this study is to collect a large amount of data that may assist in addressing the gap in knowledge of understanding pupillometer readings using a pupillometer device. The aim of this project is to establish normative values for pupillometer data. item.title: Real-time NOMA Evaluation
item.description: Alerts related to outlier clinician behavior are generated in real-time by an intelligent system continuously scraping EHR (electronic health record) data. These alerts are passed to the bedside and their potential impact on bedside clinical behavior is evaluated.

item.title: Clinical Trial of CG-BM1 Allogeneic Human Bone Marrow Mesenchymal Stem Cell Injection in the Treatment of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
item.description: 1. To evaluate the safety and tolerability of CG-BM1 for the treatment of patients with Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome. 2. To observe the preliminary effectiveness of CG-BM1 in treating Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome patients.

item.title: Pulmonary-Specific Enteral Nutrition in Mechanically Ventilated Patients With Pneumonia
item.description: Pneumonia is a major cause of critical illness and respiratory failure, particularly among patients requiring invasive mechanical ventilation. These patients frequently experience systemic inflammation and metabolic disturbances, which can be assessed using the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and blood lactate levels. item.title: Comparison of Corticosteroids vs Placebo on Duration of Ventilatory Support During Severe Acute Exacerbations of COPD Patients in the ICU
item.description: The main objective of this study is to determine if the systemic (intravenous) administration of corticosteroids, as compared to placebo, increases the number of ventilator-free days (VFD) and alive at day 28 in COPD patients admitted to an ICU, a step-up unit or a respiratory care unit for an acute on chronic respiratory failure (ACRF) requiring ventilatory support, either invasive or non-invasive.

item.title: Protocol for Rapid Onset of Mobilization in Patients With Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury II (PROMPT-SCI II) Trial
item.description: Spinal cord injuries (SCI) are among the most catastrophic survivable events experienced by human beings. Affected individuals remain with lifelong neurological impairment involving motor, sensory, bladder and bowel functions, which in turn impacts quality of life and independence. item.description: Pneumonia is a lung infection that can cause serious complications, especially when accompanied by sepsis. Sepsis can trigger excessive inflammation and abnormal blood clotting, potentially leading to organ damage and delayed recovery. Two blood markers, D-dimer and interleukin-6 (IL-6), may increase in patients with these conditions. item.description: Many patients in intensive care (ICU) need help to breathe on a breathing machine and need pain killers and sedatives to keep them comfortable and pain free. However, keeping patients too deeply sedated can make their ICU stay longer, can cause ICU confusion (delirium) and afterwards may cause distressing memories. item.description: This is a pilot feasibility study examining the use of immersive virtual reality (VR) in adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients. The study evaluates whether brief, non-interactive VR sessions delivered using a commercially available standalone head-mounted display with calming, nature-based content can be delivered safely and effectively within routine SICU workflow. item.description: EXTUBE is an international, multicentre, prospective cohort study evaluating the incidence, risk factors, and outcomes of extubation-related complications and describing clinical practices related to extubation after general anesthesia or after critical illness in the operating room (OR), out of OR anesthesia location or intensive care unit (ICU).

item.description: Sedation is given to intensive care unit (ICU) patients to treat discomfort, anxiety, agitation, and to help facilitate care, particularly when they require a breathing tube. item.description: In this study aimed to compare bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA)-guided fluid resuscitation with conventional fluid management strategies in patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) following major surgery. item.title: Efficacy and Safety of Methylene Blue in the Treatment of Severe Septic Shock
item.description: The goal of this clinical trial is to investigate whether methylene blue injection can safely and effectively improve the survival rate of patients with severe septic shock, shorten the duration of norepinephrine use, reduce the dosage of vasopressors, promptly correct hemodynamics, and improve tissue perfusion and organ function impairment.

item.description: Antimicrobial resistance AMR is an emerging global threat to human health, and intensive care units (ICUs) are a 'hot spot' for the emergence and diffusion of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria. ICU-acquired colonization and infection with MDR bacteria (ICU-MDR-col and ICU-MDR-inf, respectively) have been associated with higher ICU length-of-stay, duration of invasive mechanical ventilation and mortality. item.description: This prospective observational pilot study will evaluate how accurately anesthesiologists can predict, before a procedure, whether an adult patient will require admission to an intensive care unit (İCU) after surgery or an endoscopic procedure. item.description: There are several practical challenges in providing oral care to intubated patients. The presence of an endotracheal tube often makes it difficult to thoroughly evaluate the oral cavity, and there is a risk of tube displacement or removal during oral care. item.title: Capillary Leak Index Versus Conventional Biomarkers in Predicting Sepsis-Related Outcomes
item.description: This study aims to evaluate the prognostic significance of CLI in predicting 28-day mortality and other outcomes in critically ill patients who develop post-operative abdominal sepsis.

item.title: Rhu-pGSN for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)
item.description: BTI-203 is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, Phase 2 proof-of-concept (POC) study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of rhu-pGSN plus standard of care (SOC) in subjects with moderate-to-severe ARDS (P/F ratio ≤150) due to pneumonia or other infections. Potential subjects hospitalized with pneumonia or other infections are to be screened within 24 hours of diagnosis of ARDS.

item.description: Critically ill patients can develop high levels of inflammation, which may contribute to organ damage, muscle loss, and difficulty recovering physical function. Fish oil contains omega-3 fatty acids that may help reduce inflammation. However, the most suitable dose of fish oil given intravenously (directly into a vein) in critically ill patients with high levels of inflammation is uncertain. item.description: Sepsis is a severe, life-threatening condition caused by an abnormal host response to infection, which includes systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, and increasing organ dysfunction. item.description: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is a latent infection virus that is widespread in the population. CMV may reactivate under certain circumstances, and its hazardous nature has been proven, especially in immunosuppressed patients. However in recent years, some studies have found that CMV reactivation also exists in apparently immunocompetent patients during their critical illness. item.description: The recommended volume resuscitation for patients with early sepsis-induced hypoperfusion is at least 30 ml/kg of crystalloid administered within the first three hours. However, this standardized approach does not account for individual patient variability and lacks personalization. item.description: This multicenter randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the efficacy of Shenfu Injection in preventing and treating ventilator dependence and ventilator-induced diaphragm dysfunction (VIDD) in critically ill adult patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation. item.title: A Communication Tool to Improve Communication in the ICU
item.description: The purpose of this study is to test the effectiveness of the Best Case/Worst Case-ICU communication tool on quality of communication, clinician moral distress, and ICU length of stay for older adults with serious traumatic injury. Investigators will follow an estimated 4500 patients aged 50 years and older who are in the ICU for 3 or more days and survey 1500 family members and up to 1600 clinicians from 8 sites nationwide.

item.description: This study will compare two commonly used methods of enteral feeding in critically ill adults: continuous feeding and intermittent feeding. We will be used ultrasound for measurement the rectus femoris cross sectional area.
